conventions.convention: Holonomies multiply links in traversal order, with the first traversed edge on the left; reverse traversal uses the inverse. Vertex transformations act by U_vw ↦ Ω_v U_vw Ω_w⁻¹.

Use normalized bi-invariant Haar Borel probability and its original finite product measures, without requiring measure completion. Full AC supplies Haar existence and implies the countable choice required for L² completeness.
Complex L² consists of almost-everywhere equivalence classes; its pairing is linear in the first variable. Gauge invariance means invariance under every vertex-group element as an L² class.
The periodic four-dimensional regulator has integers N_s,N_t ≥ 3, a > 0, g₀ > 0, β = 4/g₀², and natural units ℏ = c = 1. Transfer kernels split each spatial action equally between adjacent steps.
The regulator is an adopted finite Euclidean model. No continuum, infinite-volume, Lorentzian spectrum, confinement, or empirical conclusion is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: Under full AC and the specified finite periodic SU(2) Wilson data, bounded Borel observable integrals are finite and 0 < Z_Λ ≤ 1. The gauge-invariant slice subspace is closed and contains the nonzero constant function. T is bounded with norm ≤ 1 and maps the kinematic space into that subspace. Cyclic products of N_t kernels reconstruct Z_Λ, including bounded slice-observable insertions.

Assuming countable choice, SU(2), with its matrix topology and standard real Lie-group structure, is a compact Hausdorff non-Abelian finite-dimensional real Lie group. Its defining representation is smooth and unitary. Every element has matrix entries α, β, −conjugate(β), conjugate(α), with |α|² + |β|² = 1; consequently half its real trace belongs to [−1,1].

Adopt the specified pure SU(2) finite periodic Euclidean Wilson regulator, normalized Haar link measure, normalized observable expectations, group-invariant spatial-slice sector, and temporally averaged one-step kernel with half the spatial action on either side.

published_dependencies.used_for: The countable-choice hypothesis inherited by the SU(2) Lie-group construction and L² completeness.
Full choice for normalized Haar existence and its implication to countable choice.
Finite-dimensional real smooth group structure and smooth multiplication and inversion.
Embedded smooth matrix-group structures on U(2) and SU(2), including smooth inclusion.
Compactness of the closed bounded SU(2) matrix subset of R⁸.
Existence and uniqueness under AC of normalized Haar probability, with right and inversion invariance.
Measurability of parameter integrals and exchange of finite-product integrations; complex integrands are handled by their real and imaginary positive and negative parts.
Finite Haar product probabilities, rectangle formulas, and uniqueness used to establish gauge-measure preservation.
Complex L² completeness under countable choice, on the original slice measure without completion assumptions.
Representative independence, L²-to-L¹ estimates on probability spaces, and the transfer contraction estimate.
The lattice-data supplier's identification of finite-product Borel and product sigma-algebras.

concerns.concern: The Statement introduces L²(SU(2)^{E_s},dμ_s) and h ∈ SU(2)^{V_s} without explicitly defining E_s or V_s. Their intended meanings are readily reconstructed as V_s = (Z/N_s Z)³ and E_s = V_s × {1,2,3}, and the later postulate states them explicitly, but that later consumer cannot supply definitions for this lemma.
